Solution: b and c. The relation d×e≡1(modϕ(n)) means there exists an integer k such that d×e−k×ϕ(n)=1. According to Bézout's Identity, a linear combination of two integers e and ϕ(n) can equal 1 if and only if their greatest common divisor (gcd) divides 1.
